question.text: For the function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> which of the following is true?

options.text: Greatest value of the function is <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math>
Greatest value of the function is <math><mn>4</mn></math>

Rolle’s Theorem is applicable to <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> in <math><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>

LMVT is not applicable to <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> in <math><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
Let, sin⁡x=t∈0,1
∴ft=t3-3t+4
Now,  f ′ t =3 t 2 −3
=3t-1t+1
∴ f ′ t ≤0 ∀t∈ 0,1
∴max⁡ft=0-0+4=4
Also, fx is continuous in 0,1 and differentiable in 0,1, hence LMVT is applicable.
But, f0≠f1, hence Rolle’s theorem is not applicable
